python3 - <<'PY'
p='system/deploy'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('# ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ─')
end=s.index('find etc/ -type d')
new='''# ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ───────────────────────────
# install-base.sh pacstraps the same list, but that only ever runs on the live
# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Ordered
# before the etc/ copy below so a host's FIRST deploy installs pam_fprintd.so
# before etc/pam.d/polkit-1 starts naming it (on later runs the file is already
# in place from the previous one, so the ordering buys nothing).
#
# An explicit host list, NOT `command -v pacman`: those are different
# predicates. kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an Arch-based one
# would sail through a capability check and be handed a kernel and a base
# metapackage. Mirrors the host case in home.nix's `hms`; docs/new-host.md step
# 0 says to add a new host to both. Hosts not listed still get the etc/ copy
# below, which means they keep a pam_fprintd line they cannot load -- fail-safe
# (polkit falls through to the password) but it logs on every polkit auth.
#
# SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1 skips just this step: a pacman failure below aborts the
# whole script, and everything after it (the attic netrc most of all, which is
# what lets the following home-manager switch download CI's closure instead of
# building locally) has nothing to do with packages.
case "${SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES:+skip}${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}" in
skip*)
  echo "system/deploy: SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES set -- not touching pacman."
  ;;
utsuho|setsuna|shiori|fujiwara)
  [ -f packages ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages is missing" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Strip comments, then split on any whitespace: one package per line is the
  # documented format, and this makes a two-names-on-one-line slip fail as two
  # packages rather than silently concatenate into one bogus name.
  mapfile -t want < <(sed 's/#.*//' packages | tr -s '[:space:]' '\\n' | sed '/^$/d')
  # mapfile returns 0 whatever the process substitution did, and `set -e` does
  # not see into it, so an empty parse has to be caught by hand -- otherwise a
  # renamed or emptied list makes this step a silent no-op, which is the exact
  # failure this file exists to fix.
  [ ${#want[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

  missing=()
  for p in "${want[@]}"; do
    # -Qq resolves virtual provides (`pacman -Qq sh` -> bash), so a
    # provider-satisfied entry is not reported missing.
    pacman -Qq -- "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
  done

  if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"
    # `--` because the list is data: a line that starts with a dash would
    # otherwise be read as a pacman option (--hookdir=, --overwrite=, --root=),
    # and this runs under sudo.
    #
    # No `--noconfirm`: pacman's default answer to "replace X with Y?" and
    # "X conflicts with Y, remove Y?" is yes, so --noconfirm would let a
    # one-line edit that looks purely additive silently REMOVE something from a
    # running host. Prompting costs a keypress only when something is actually
    # missing.
    #
    # No `-y` either: installing against a freshly refreshed db without

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ───────────────────────────
# install-base.sh pacstraps the same list, but that only ever runs on the live
# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Do this
# before the etc/ copy below: etc/pam.d/polkit-1 names pam_fprintd.so, and a
# stack referencing a module that isn't installed yet logs a load error on
# every auth.
#
# Deliberately no `-y`: refreshing the sync db without upgrading is a partial
# upgrade, the one way to break an Arch box. `-S` uses the db as it stands, so
# on a host that hasn't been updated in a while the download can 404 on a
# version the mirrors dropped -- that is what the hint below is for.
# Guarded on pacman existing: this script also runs on the darwin host and on
# boxes we do not own the OS of (kyuusaku), where the etc/ bits below are the
# only part that applies.
if command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mapfile -t want < <(sed -e 's/#.*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]//g' -e '/^$/d' packages)
  missing=()
  for p in "${want[@]}"; do
    pacman -Qq "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
  done
  if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"
    sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm "${missing[@]}" || {
      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed; if it 404'd, run 'sudo pacman -Syu' and retry." >&2
      exit 1
    }
  fi
fi

find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# only part that applies.

    echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"

      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed; if it 404'd, run 'sudo pacman -Syu' and retry." >&2

# ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ───────────────────────────
# install-base.sh pacstraps the same list, but that only ever runs on the live
# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Ordered
# before the etc/ copy below so a host's FIRST deploy installs pam_fprintd.so
# before etc/pam.d/polkit-1 starts naming it. On later runs that file is already
# in place from the previous deploy, so the ordering buys nothing.
#
# An explicit host list, NOT `command -v pacman`: those are different
# predicates. kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an Arch-based one
# would sail through a capability check and be handed a kernel and a base
# metapackage. Mirrors the host case in home.nix's `hms`; docs/new-host.md step
# 0 says to add a new host to both. A host that is not listed still gets the
# etc/ copy below, so it keeps a pam_fprintd line it cannot load -- fail-safe
# (polkit falls through to the password) at the price of a log line per auth.
#
# SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1 skips just this step. A pacman failure below aborts the
# whole script, and nothing after it is about packages -- least of all the attic
# netrc, which is what lets the home-manager switch after this download CI's
# closure instead of building locally.
case "${SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES:+skip-}${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}" in
skip-*)
  echo "system/deploy: SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES set -- not touching pacman."
  ;;
utsuho | setsuna | shiori | fujiwara)
  [ -f packages ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages is missing" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Strip comments, then split on any whitespace. One package per line is the
  # documented format; splitting rather than deleting whitespace means a
  # two-names-on-one-line slip fails as two packages instead of silently
  # concatenating into one bogus name.
  mapfile -t want < <(sed 's/#.*//' packages | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d')
  # mapfile returns 0 whatever the process substitution did, and neither `set
  # -e` nor pipefail sees inside one, so an empty parse has to be caught by
  # hand. Without this a renamed or emptied list makes this step a silent
  # no-op -- the exact failure the list was added to fix.
  [ ${#want[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

  missing=()
  for p in "${want[@]}"; do
    # -Qq resolves virtual provides (`pacman -Qq sh` answers bash), so an entry
    # satisfied by a provider is not reported missing.
    pacman -Qq -- "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
  done

    echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"
    # `--` because the list is data: a line starting with a dash would
    # otherwise be read as a pacman option (--hookdir=, --overwrite=, --root=),
    # and this runs under sudo.
    #
    # No `--noconfirm`: pacman's default answer to "replace X with Y?" and to
    # "X conflicts with Y, remove Y?" is yes, so --noconfirm would let a
    # one-line edit that reads as purely additive silently REMOVE a package
    # from a running host. Prompting costs a keypress only when something is
    # actually missing.
    #
    # No `-y` either: installing against a just-refreshed db without upgrading
    # is the partial-upgrade footgun. `-S` against the db as it stands resolves
    # the version matching the libraries already installed, which is the safe
    # direction -- at the price of a possible 404 where the db predates a mirror
    # cleanup, hence the hint.
    sudo pacman -S --needed -- "${missing[@]}" || {
      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed. If it 404'd, the sync db is stale:" >&2
      echo "  sudo pacman -Syu" >&2
      echo "then retry -- or SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1 to get on with the rest." >&2
      exit 1
    }
  fi
  ;;
*)
  echo "system/deploy: ${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)} is not one of our Arch hosts -- skipping host packages."
  ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ───────────────────────────
# install-base.sh pacstraps the same list, but that only ever runs on the live
# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Do this
# before the etc/ copy below: etc/pam.d/polkit-1 names pam_fprintd.so, and a
# stack referencing a module that isn't installed yet logs a load error on
# every auth.
#
# Deliberately no `-y`: refreshing the sync db without upgrading is a partial
# upgrade, the one way to break an Arch box. `-S` uses the db as it stands, so
# on a host that hasn't been updated in a while the download can 404 on a
# version the mirrors dropped -- that is what the hint below is for.
# Guarded on pacman existing: this script also runs on the darwin host and on
# boxes we do not own the OS of (kyuusaku), where the etc/ bits below are the
# only part that applies.
if command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mapfile -t want < <(sed -e 's/#.*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]//g' -e '/^$/d' packages)
  missing=()
  for p in "${want[@]}"; do
    pacman -Qq "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
  done
  if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"
    sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm "${missing[@]}" || {
      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed; if it 404'd, run 'sudo pacman -Syu' and retry." >&2
      exit 1
    }
  fi
fi

find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# polkit only scans /usr/share/polkit-1/actions for action definitions, which
# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

# ── gnome-keyring: let the home-manager unit own the daemon ───────────────────
# The login collection can only be unlocked at daemon startup, so home-manager
# runs its own gnome-keyring.service whose ExecStart unseals the passphrase from
# the TPM (see gnome-keyring-tpm in home.nix). Mask Arch's packaged units so a
# second, *locked* daemon can't be started behind our back -- its socket unit
# listens on %t/keyring/control and would socket-activate one on any control-op.
# This is only half the job: the D-Bus activation files in /usr/share also start
# a locked daemon, and systemd masking does nothing about those. They are
# shadowed from ~/.local/share/dbus-1/services by home.nix.
sudo rm -f /etc/systemd/user/sockets.target.wants/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket
sudo ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/user/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket
sudo ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/user/gnome-keyring-daemon.service

# Unsealing the gnome-keyring passphrase reads /dev/tpmrm0, which is root:tss 0660.
# Takes effect at next login, not in the current session.
if ! id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx tss; then
  sudo gpasswd -a "$USER" tss
fi

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
# systemd-oomd parses oomd.conf (and its drop-ins) once at startup, so a changed
# etc/systemd/oomd.conf.d/* must be followed by an actual restart. `enable --now`
# is NOT enough: --now only *starts* a stopped unit, so on a host where oomd is
# already running it is a silent no-op and the new limits sit on disk unapplied.
# `restart` covers both cases (starts it if stopped) and kills nothing on its way
# through -- oomd holds no state worth preserving across a reload.
sudo systemctl enable systemd-oomd
sudo systemctl restart systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),
# then install to /etc as root. The token is never printed.
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json}"

# Plain upstream nix only reads /etc/nix/nix.conf; pull in nix.custom.conf so the
# substituter + trusted key take effect. Idempotent, and a no-op on Determinate
# (whose own nix.conf already includes it, so the grep matches and we skip).
if ! sudo grep -qF 'nix.custom.conf' /etc/nix/nix.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '!include nix.custom.conf' | sudo tee -a /etc/nix/nix.conf >/dev/null
fi

sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/determinate/netrc.custom
sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/netrc

# ── remote builder: SSH key the nix daemon uses to reach mari ─────────────────
# nix.custom.conf delegates aarch64-darwin builds to sauyon@mari-1 over Tailscale;
# the daemon (root) authenticates with this key. Private key is sops-encrypted in
# ../secrets.yaml; install root-owned, 0600. Never printed.
sops -d --extract '["mariBuilderKey"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/mari-builder-key

# Pick up the new substituter, trusted key, netrc, and builder.
sudo systemctl restart nix-daemon

# ── tailscaled: patched build from this flake (Linux only) ───────────────────
# Tailscale SSH calls logind CreateSession before the user's shell runs, so for a
# systemd-homed user whose LUKS home is still locked it starts user@<uid>.service
# against homed's fallback home ("/") and permanently breaks that user manager's
# unit search path for the rest of the boot. The patch makes tailscaled ask homed
# for the user's state first and skip session creation when the home isn't active.
# See ../patches/tailscale-ssh-skip-logind-session-for-locked-homed-user.patch
#
# Build as the invoking user (root's nix may lack flakes and our substituters),
# then have root pin the result. A symlink placed directly in /nix/var/nix/gcroots
# is a permanent GC root, and we reuse it as the stable path tailscaled.service
# references -- it must resolve at boot, i.e. outside the encrypted home.
if [[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]]; then
  ts_out="$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$(cd .. && pwd)#tailscale-patched")"
  sudo ln -sfn "${ts_out}" /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched
  # The CLI too: /usr/bin/tailscale belongs to the distro package, which this
  # replaces. The wrapper dispatches on argv[0], so a symlink named `tailscale`
  # gets CLI behaviour rather than the daemon.
  sudo install -d /usr/local/bin
  sudo ln -sfn /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched/bin/tailscale /usr/local/bin/tailscale
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl restart tailscaled
fi

lines: # ── host packages: converge pacman onto ./packages ───────────────────────────
# install-base.sh pacstraps the same list, but that only ever runs on the live
-# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Do this
-# before the etc/ copy below: etc/pam.d/polkit-1 names pam_fprintd.so, and a
-# stack referencing a module that isn't installed yet logs a load error on
-# every auth.
+# ISO, so a package added after a host was built never reaches it. Ordered
+# before the etc/ copy below so a host's FIRST deploy installs pam_fprintd.so
+# before etc/pam.d/polkit-1 starts naming it. On later runs that file is already
+# in place from the previous deploy, so the ordering buys nothing.
-# Deliberately no `-y`: refreshing the sync db without upgrading is a partial
-# upgrade, the one way to break an Arch box. `-S` uses the db as it stands, so
-# on a host that hasn't been updated in a while the download can 404 on a
-# version the mirrors dropped -- that is what the hint below is for.
-# Guarded on pacman existing: this script also runs on the darwin host and on
-# boxes we do not own the OS of (kyuusaku), where the etc/ bits below are the
-# only part that applies.
-if command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-  mapfile -t want < <(sed -e 's/#.*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]//g' -e '/^$/d' packages)
+# An explicit host list, NOT `command -v pacman`: those are different
+# predicates. kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an Arch-based one
+# would sail through a capability check and be handed a kernel and a base
+# metapackage. Mirrors the host case in home.nix's `hms`; docs/new-host.md step
+# 0 says to add a new host to both. A host that is not listed still gets the
+# etc/ copy below, so it keeps a pam_fprintd line it cannot load -- fail-safe
+# (polkit falls through to the password) at the price of a log line per auth.
+# SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1 skips just this step. A pacman failure below aborts the
+# whole script, and nothing after it is about packages -- least of all the attic
+# netrc, which is what lets the home-manager switch after this download CI's
+# closure instead of building locally.
+case "${SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES:+skip-}${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}" in
+skip-*)
+  echo "system/deploy: SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES set -- not touching pacman."
+utsuho | setsuna | shiori | fujiwara)
+  [ -f packages ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages is missing" >&2; exit 1; }
+  # Strip comments, then split on any whitespace. One package per line is the
+  # documented format; splitting rather than deleting whitespace means a
+  # two-names-on-one-line slip fails as two packages instead of silently
+  # concatenating into one bogus name.
+  mapfile -t want < <(sed 's/#.*//' packages | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d')
+  # mapfile returns 0 whatever the process substitution did, and neither `set
+  # -e` nor pipefail sees inside one, so an empty parse has to be caught by
+  # hand. Without this a renamed or emptied list makes this step a silent
+  # no-op -- the exact failure the list was added to fix.
+  [ ${#want[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "system/deploy: ./packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
missing=()
for p in "${want[@]}"; do
-    pacman -Qq "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
+    # -Qq resolves virtual provides (`pacman -Qq sh` answers bash), so an entry
+    # satisfied by a provider is not reported missing.
+    pacman -Qq -- "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
echo "system/deploy: installing missing host packages: ${missing[*]}"
-    sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm "${missing[@]}" || {
-      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed; if it 404'd, run 'sudo pacman -Syu' and retry." >&2
+    # `--` because the list is data: a line starting with a dash would
+    # otherwise be read as a pacman option (--hookdir=, --overwrite=, --root=),
+    # and this runs under sudo.
+    # No `--noconfirm`: pacman's default answer to "replace X with Y?" and to
+    # "X conflicts with Y, remove Y?" is yes, so --noconfirm would let a
+    # one-line edit that reads as purely additive silently REMOVE a package
+    # from a running host. Prompting costs a keypress only when something is
+    # actually missing.
+    # No `-y` either: installing against a just-refreshed db without upgrading
+    # is the partial-upgrade footgun. `-S` against the db as it stands resolves
+    # the version matching the libraries already installed, which is the safe
+    # direction -- at the price of a possible 404 where the db predates a mirror
+    # cleanup, hence the hint.
+    sudo pacman -S --needed -- "${missing[@]}" || {
+      echo "system/deploy: pacman failed. If it 404'd, the sync db is stale:" >&2
+      echo "  sudo pacman -Syu" >&2
+      echo "then retry -- or SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1 to get on with the rest." >&2
exit 1
fi
-fi
+  echo "system/deploy: ${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)} is not one of our Arch hosts -- skipping host packages."
+esac
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

Given the step is "install some packages that are nice to have", warn-and-continue (or running it *after* the /etc steps, accepting A6's pacman-ownership caveat) is the proportionate behavior; aborting the secrets provisioning is not. Nothing here leaves the host *inconsistently* configured in a dangerous way — deploy is idempotent and rerunnable — but it does leave it half-configured and, on a fresh-host bootstrap, quietly much slower.

That is a partial upgrade arrived at by a different door, and neither the comment nor the hint mentions it. The comment states the reasoning as settled ("the one way to break an Arch box") when the chosen alternative shares the hazard.
  
  **B3 — nit. `system/deploy:29`: the `command -v pacman` guard is the only OS guard in a file that is otherwise unconditionally Arch+systemd.** Covered under A6. The guard is correct for what it does (a pacman-less host skips the block cleanly and nothing downstream reads `want`/`missing`), so nothing is broken downstream by the guard itself; the problem is that its comment claims the script degrades gracefully on non-Arch hosts, which it does not, and that "has pacman" is the wrong predicate for "is a host we own" (A3).
  
  **B4 — nit. `install/install-base.sh:27`: the abort message is slightly wrong and unhelpfully vague.** "no packages list beside $here or in ../system" interpolates a *directory* after "beside" ("beside /root"), and it does not print the two paths actually tried. This message is the one the operator sees over `ssh -t` from `mise run host:install` with nothing else on screen; naming `/root/packages` and `/root/../system/packages` would make the scp-didn't-land case self-diagnosing.
  
  **B5 — Important (same defect as A2, stated as an error-handling claim). "fails while the target is still intact" is only true for the file-missing case.** The early resolve at `:22-28` is genuinely before `[[ -b $DISK ]]`, before the passphrase prompts, and before `sgdisk -Z` — good, and the abort path does fire (verified). But the checks it performs are existence only. Empty list, unreadable file, fused line, typo'd name: all first surface at `pacstrap` (`:77`) or later, after `sgdisk -Z` + `luksFormat` + `mkfs`. For a script whose entire safety story is "fail before the disk," the pre-flight is one assertion short.

Consequence is mild (one-time reinstall of nix-duplicated tools), but the file's own rule is the thing that will be cited when the next line is added, and it is already wrong.
  
  ## B. ERROR HANDLING
  
  **B1 — Important. `system/deploy:37-40`: a pacman failure aborts the entire deploy before any /etc convergence — a robustness regression against dcaecea.**
  `exit 1` in the `||` block kills the script at line 40, so the etc/ copy (`:44-45`), the Bitwarden polkit action (`:50`), the gnome-keyring masking (`:62-64`), the `tss` group add (`:68`), the oomd restart (`:79-80`), `/etc/nix/nix.conf` include + attic netrc + mari builder key (`:100-116`), the nix-daemon restart (`:119`) and the patched tailscaled (`:133-142`) all stop happening. Scenario: setsuna, db three weeks old, `fprintd` legitimately missing → `pacman -S fprintd` 404s on a dropped version → deploy exits 1 → the host keeps its stale `/etc`, and (the part that actually hurts) never gets `/etc/nix/netrc`, so `mise run bootstrap`'s next step, the home-manager switch, cannot authenticate to the private attic cache and compiles the closure from source — the exact failure the ordering comment at `mise.toml:192-193` was written to prevent. Before this commit, a package problem could not do that. Given the step is "install some packages that are nice to have", warn-and-continue (or running it *after* the /etc steps, accepting A6's pacman-ownership caveat) is the proportionate behavior; aborting the secrets provisioning is not. Nothing here leaves the host *inconsistently* configured in a dangerous way — deploy is idempotent and rerunnable — but it does leave it half-configured and, on a fresh-host bootstrap, quietly much slower.
  
  **B2 — Important. `system/deploy:38`: the hint names one failure mode; most real failures print it anyway, and the `-Sy` rationale is only half right.**
  `sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm` reaches that `echo` for every nonzero exit, so all of these print "if it 404'd, run 'sudo pacman -Syu' and retry": db lock held by a concurrent pacman or a pacman hook (`unable to lock database`), the sudo password being refused or timing out (deploy is run interactively as the user; only during `bootstrap` is `99-bootstrap` NOPASSWD in place), no network / unreachable mirror, `/` or `/var/cache/pacman` full, and unresolvable conflicts — note `--noconfirm` takes the *default* answer, which is **No** for "remove conflicting package?", so a host with a conflicting provider installed (the classic being `bluez-utils-compat` vs `system/packages:58` `bluez-utils`) aborts with a conflict error and gets told to run `-Syu`, which will not help. "`pacman -Syu` and retry" is also non-trivial advice on Arch (full system upgrade, possible reboot) to dispense for what may be a lock file.
  Separately, the deliberate omission of `-y` (commit message; `system/deploy:22-25`) prevents a db refresh but does **not** prevent a partial upgrade: `-S` resolves dependencies against the db *as it stands*, and if that db is newer than the installed system — someone ran `pacman -Sy` by hand, or any tool did — installing `fprintd` pulls `libfprint` and whatever newer `glibc`/`polkit`/`dbus` it depends on, upgrading those packages alone. That is a partial upgrade arrived at by a different door, and neither the comment nor the hint mentions it. The comment states the reasoning as settled ("the one way to break an Arch box") when the chosen alternative shares the hazard.
  
  **B3 — nit. `system/deploy:29`: the `command -v pacman` guard is the only OS guard in a file that is otherwise unconditionally Arch+systemd.** Covered under A6. The guard is correct for what it does (a pacman-less host skips the block cleanly and nothing downstream reads `want`/`missing`), so nothing is broken downstream by the guard itself; the problem is that its comment claims the script degrades gracefully on non-Arch hosts, which it does not, and that "has pacman" is the wrong predicate for "is a host we own" (A3).
  
  **B4 — nit. `install/install-base.sh:27`: the abort message is slightly wrong and unhelpfully vague.** "no packages list beside $here or in ../system" interpolates a *directory* after "beside" ("beside /root"), and it does not print the two paths actually tried. This message is the one the operator sees over `ssh -t` from `mise run host:install` with nothing else on screen; naming `/root/packages` and `/root/../system/packages` would make the scp-didn't-land case self-diagnosing.
  
  **B5 — Important (same defect as A2, stated as an error-handling claim). "fails while the target is still intact" is only true for the file-missing case.** The early resolve at `:22-28` is genuinely before `[[ -b $DISK ]]`, before the passphrase prompts, and before `sgdisk -Z` — good, and the abort path does fire (verified). But the checks it performs are existence only. Empty list, unreadable file, fused line, typo'd name: all first surface at `pacstrap` (`:77`) or later, after `sgdisk -Z` + `luksFormat` + `mkfs`. For a script whose entire safety story is "fail before the disk," the pre-flight is one assertion short.

  ## Verifiability
  
  Verifiable by dry run, and I did: the sed parse against the real file (exact, 30 names); the CRLF / inline-comment / fused-line edge cases; `pacman -Qq` on a provides name, a group name, and `base-devel`; `base-devel`'s package-vs-group status; the `for`-loop errexit question; empty/unset array expansion under `set -u`; the mise `dir` → scp path arithmetic (static, but conclusive); pre/post package-set equality.
  
  Verifiable by dry run and *not* done anywhere in the repo: `pacman -S --print --needed -- <list>` as a deploy pre-flight (would turn B1/B2's late abort into an early, accurate diagnosis); `pacman -Sp --print-format '%n' -- "${pkgs[@]}"` in install-base.sh (would catch A2/A5 before `sgdisk -Z`); `shellcheck` on `system/deploy` and `install/install-base.sh` (`.forgejo/workflows/` contains only `nix-home.yml` and `vulnix-scan.yml`; there is no shell lint, no shfmt, no pre-commit hook, no tests directory).
  
  What the repo does **not** verify at all: that `system/packages` parses to a non-empty list; that every name in it exists in the repos (a typo is discovered on the live ISO after the disk is wiped, or mid-deploy on a real host); that the install-base.sh inline hardware set plus `system/packages` still equals what a host needs (the only guard is review); that the list is appropriate per host (kernel variant, headless, AMD vs Intel, reader present); and that the fprintd chain actually works end to end — enrollment is manual (`docs/new-host.md:113-117`), hyprlock reaches fprintd over D-Bus rather than PAM, so an unenrolled host still silently no-ops exactly as before, and nothing in the repo detects that state. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Base Arch install for a new host, run as root on the archiso live system:
3	#   HOST=<name> DISK=/dev/nvme0n1 bash install-base.sh
4	# Normally invoked via `mise run host:install <ip> <host>`.
5	# Full-disk LUKS2 -> btrfs, systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user sauyon.
6	# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
7	# unattended.
8	set -euo pipefail
9	
10	DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
11	part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
12	ESP=$(part 1)
13	CRYPT=$(part 2)
14	HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
15	USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}
16	TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}
17	
18	# The package list is shared with system/deploy -- see system/packages for the
19	# split. `mise run host:install` scp's it next to this script; a plain repo
20	# checkout finds it one level up. Resolved here, before anything touches the
21	# disk, so a missing list fails while the target is still intact.
22	here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	pkglist=
24	for c in "$here/packages" "$here/../system/packages"; do
25	  [ -f "$c" ] && { pkglist=$c; break; }
26	done
27	[ -n "$pkglist" ] || { echo "install-base.sh: no packages list beside $here or in ../system" >&2; exit 1; }
28	mapfile -t pkgs < <(sed -e 's/#.*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]//g' -e '/^$/d' "$pkglist")
29	
30	# Refuse to touch a disk that already has partitions; wipe it by hand first
31	# (sgdisk -Z) if you really mean it.
32	[[ -b $DISK ]] || { echo "$DISK is not a block device" >&2; exit 1; }

# Two package lists, both resolved HERE -- before the passphrase prompts and

# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done
  echo "install-base.sh: no readable package list at any of: $*" >&2
  return 1
}

mapfile -t pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages" "$here/../system/packages")
mapfile -t boot_pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages-install-only")

# not see inside one -- so the counts are checked by hand. Without this an empty
# list pacstraps almost nothing, and the first sign of trouble is arch-chroot
# failing for want of a shell, long after the disk has been wiped.
[ ${#pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: system/packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ${#boot_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: packages-install-only parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

CRYPT=$(part 2)

editor no

options rd.luks.name=${luks_uuid}=root rd.luks.options=discard root=/dev/mapper/root rootflags=subvol=@ rw

[tasks.bootstrap]
description = "Set up this host: Determinate Nix, sops key via Keycloak sign-in (URL + QR), system:deploy, home-manager switch, tailscale. Fresh box: bootstrap or curl -fsSL ko.ag/bootstrap | bash"
tools = { sops = "latest" }
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
host="$(uname -n)"; host="${host%%.*}"
repo="{{config_root}}"
# install-base.sh leaves passwordless sudo for this; drop it however we exit.
trap 'sudo -n rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

if [ ! -d /nix/var/nix/profiles/default ]; then
  curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
    | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh

# sops key. sops-nix, system/deploy and `mise run sops` read
# ~/.config/sops/gcp-key.json. A new host fetches it from the cluster: a
# Keycloak device-code sign-in (URL + QR, approve on your phone, nothing to
# type), then the resulting token reads Secret bootstrap/sops-gcp-key from the
# apiserver. The Secret is put there once, from a host that has the key:
#   kubectl create namespace bootstrap
#   kubectl -n bootstrap create secret generic sops-gcp-key --from-file=gcp-key.json=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json
key="$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json"
if [ ! -s "$key" ]; then
  nixbin() { echo "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$repo" "nixpkgs#$1^bin")/bin/$1"; }
  jq="$(nixbin jq)"; qrencode="$(nixbin qrencode)"
  issuer="https://keycloak.ko.ag/realms/ko"
  dev="$(curl -fsS -d client_id=kubectl -d 'scope=openid email profile' "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/auth/device")"
  url="$("$jq" -r .verification_uri_complete <<<"$dev")"
  device_code="$("$jq" -r .device_code <<<"$dev")"
  interval="$("$jq" -r '.interval // 5' <<<"$dev")"
  echo
  echo "Sign in to fetch the sops key: $url"
  "$qrencode" -t ansiutf8 "$url"
  echo "Waiting for approval..."
  while :; do
    sleep "$interval"
    tok="$(curl -sS -d client_id=kubectl -d "device_code=$device_code" \
      -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code \
      "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/token")"
    case "$("$jq" -r '.error // empty' <<<"$tok")" in
      "") break ;;
      authorization_pending) ;;
      slow_down) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
      *) echo "bootstrap: sign-in failed: $("$jq" -r '.error_description // .error' <<<"$tok")" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  id_token="$("$jq" -r .id_token <<<"$tok")"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$key")"
  (
    umask 077
    curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $id_token" \
      https://k8s.ko.ag/api/v1/namespaces/bootstrap/secrets/sops-gcp-key \
      | "$jq" -er '.data["gcp-key.json"]' | base64 -d > "$key.tmp"
  )
  mv "$key.tmp" "$key"
  echo "bootstrap: sops key fetched."
fi

# system/deploy first: it installs the attic netrc, so the switch below pulls
# CI's build of this host instead of compiling it.
"$repo/system/deploy"

if command -v home-manager >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  home-manager switch --flake "$repo#$host"
else
  nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch -b pre-hm --flake "$repo#$host"
fi

sudo tailscale status >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo tailscale up

echo "bootstrap: done. Log in again (or exec zsh -l) to pick up the new profile."
'''

config="$(uname -n)"; config="${config%%.*}"

'''

# New host runbook

From a blank machine to an Arch box running this flake. Everything after
booting the stick happens over SSH, so it can be driven from another machine.

The result: full-disk LUKS2 → btrfs (`@`, `@home`, `@nix`, `@log`, `@cache`,
zstd), systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user `sauyon` in `wheel`, Determinate Nix,
and the first Home Manager switch done.

## 0. Register the host in the flake

Pick a hostname, then in this repo:

- `flake.nix`: add `homeConfigurations.<host> = linuxHome { hostname = "<host>"; gui = true; };`
  (`gpu = "amd"`/`"nvidia"` only if it has one; anything else can be left out).
- `home.nix`: add `<host>` to the `hms` CI case (`utsuho|setsuna|...`) if it
  gets a CI job, and to whichever scale knob its panel wants: `hidpi` for 1.25
  app-level scaling, or `laptopScale` for a 2x compositor scale on `eDP-1`.
  Pick one — they multiply.
- `.forgejo/workflows/nix-home.yml`: add
  `.#homeConfigurations.<host>.activationPackage` to the build step.

Commit and push; CI will have the closure in attic by the time you need it.

## 1. Build the install ISO

`install/` holds an archiso profile overlay on top of the stock `releng`
profile. The ISO auto-joins one Wi-Fi network (iwd) and allows key-only root
SSH, advertised over mDNS as `archiso.local`. Needs Docker (Docker Desktop is
fine; the build runs in a privileged `archlinux` container).

```bash

Then log in again (`exec zsh -l` on a console that predates the switch) and
`start-hyprland`.

## 5. Afterwards

- Enroll a fingerprint if the box has a reader: `fprintd-enroll`, then
  `fprintd-list $USER` to confirm. The enrollment is root state in
  `/var/lib/fprint`, per host, and nothing in this repo can carry it over. It
  unlocks hyprlock and the polkit/Bitwarden prompt; `sudo` and TTY login stay
  password-only on purpose.
- Turn Secure Boot back on only if you also set up signing (sbctl); the base
  install doesn't sign anything.
- Delete the ISO, or keep it private: it has the Wi-Fi passphrase in it.

input.content:
system: converge host packages onto a shared list, and install fprintd

pacstrap's list in install-base.sh was the only place host packages were
declared, and it runs on the live ISO -- so a package added after a host was
built never reached it. fprintd is what that cost: hyprlock's
fingerprint.enabled and etc/pam.d/polkit-1's pam_fprintd were wired up months
ago, but nothing ever installed the daemon, so a fresh shiori has the Goodix
reader (27c6:609c) sitting there with no fprintd, no /var/lib/fprint, and a
fingerprint prompt that silently no-ops.

fprintd cannot come from nix: the host's PAM dlopens pam_fprintd.so by bare
name out of /usr/lib/security, fprintd is a root-run system D-Bus service, and
its enrollments are root state under /var.

Split the declaration by lifetime rather than keeping one list:

  system/packages               what every host must have. system/deploy
                                installs whatever is missing on each run, which
                                is the half that reaches setsuna/utsuho/shiori
                                rather than only the next new box.
  install/packages-install-only base, base-devel, the kernel, and enough shell
                                to reach bootstrap. Pacstrapped once, never
                                re-enforced -- converging `linux` would install
                                a second, stock kernel on a host that had moved
                                to -lts or -zen, and git/vim/fzf are home.nix's
                                job once it exists.
  HW_PKGS / --hw                ucode and video drivers, which would be wrong
                                rather than merely unused on the other
                                architecture. Defaults to Intel; utsuho and
                                fujiwara are AMD, so the runbook now says to
                                pass it.

The converge step is deliberately conservative. An explicit host allow-list,
not `command -v pacman`: kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an
Arch-based one would sail through a capability check and be handed a kernel.
`--` before the package arguments, because the list is data and a leading dash
would otherwise be read as a pacman option under sudo. No `--noconfirm`, whose
default answer to "X conflicts with Y, remove Y?" is yes -- a line that reads as
purely additive should not be able to remove a package from a running host. No
`-y`, since refreshing the db and installing without upgrading is the
partial-upgrade footgun. And a pacman failure warns rather than aborts: nothing
later in system/deploy is about packages, least of all the attic netrc that
keeps the next home-manager switch from compiling the world.

PAM wiring is unchanged as text, but not in effect, which is worth saying
plainly: polkit-1's `auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so` was inert while the module
could not be dlopen'd, and installing fprintd makes it live. A fingerprint now
short-circuits system-auth, pam_faillock included, for polkit auth_self. sudo
and TTY login stay password-only. Noted in the stack's comment and the runbook,
along with enrollment staying manual per host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}

Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Dropping the flag's `default=` and letting `${HW_PKGS:-…}` be the single source would collapse it (at the cost of `usage_hw` being empty, so you'd pass `HW_PKGS` only when set).

Two comments now overstate deploy's reach after A3's allow-list.** `system/packages:2` — "system/deploy converges pacman onto this file on each run" — and `install-base.sh:20` — "system/deploy enforces that file on every box" — are both true only of the four allow-listed hosts. Small, but the allow-list is a deliberate safety property and these two sentences read as though it isn't there.

The *effect* the sentence describes (password only, no fingerprint offered) is correct, so nothing behaves differently. Flagging it because the amendment added ten lines directly beneath it without correcting it, and because B1's false claim grows from the same misconception about where Arch keeps packaged PAM stacks. Fixing both together is one edit.
  
  **B7 — no finding. Split faithfulness confirmed** (see table). Also confirmed the two format claims the new comments make: `pacman -Qq` does resolve virtual provides (`pacman -Qq sh` → `bash`) and does **not** resolve groups (`pacman -Qq vulkan-devel` → "package … was not found"), so `system/packages:25-27` is accurate, including the warning that a group line would read as missing every run.
  
  **B8 — no finding on the amended commit message, with one inherited caveat.** It is materially more precise than round 1's: "unchanged as text, but not in effect" is exactly right; the harmful/inert framing matches the code; the `--` / no-`--noconfirm` / no-`-y` / warn-not-abort paragraph each match what `deploy` actually does; the kernel rationale is sound; "utsuho and fujiwara are AMD" matches `flake.nix:62,84`. It does **not** repeat B1's false ordering claim, so that falsehood is confined to deploy's comment. The single caveat is the zsh omission noted in B2.
  
  **B9 — nit. Discoverability.** `mise.toml`'s `system:deploy` description still reads "Install missing host packages and system-level files…" with no hint that the package half is allow-listed and skippable. Adding "(allow-listed hosts; `SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1` to skip)" would put the two new behaviours where a reader of `mise tasks` will find them.
  
  ---
  
  ## Bottom line
  
  Nine of the twelve fixes hold cleanly, and A4 and A5 in particular are now better-documented than I asked for. Three things to act on before this lands:
  
  1. **B1** — the ordering comment documents a mechanism that does not exist, and contradicts `system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1:2`. Highest-value fix; it's a comment-only edit, and B6 rides along with it.
  2. **A2-new / A1-new** — `HW_PKGS` is the one new untrusted-shaped input in the change, and it passes through both an unquoted remote shell string and a `pacstrap` argv with no `--`. Both are small, local fixes.
  3. **A3-new** — `${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}` falls back to a binary absent from these hosts and absent from both package lists; `uname -n` is the repo's own convention three other places.
  
  **B2** (zsh) is latent and a judgement call, but it is the only entry the new split's rule misfiles, so it's worth a decision rather than a silent pass. Everything else is nit-level.
  
</agent-message>

The rest of the split is well-judged, and the kernel argument at `packages-install-only:8-10` (converging `linux` would install a second stock kernel alongside `-lts`/`-zen`, run the mkinitcpio hook, fill `/boot`) is the strongest single piece of reasoning in the change.
  
  **B3 — nit. `HW_PKGS` has two defaults.** `install-base.sh:25` (`${HW_PKGS:-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}`) and the `--hw` flag default in `mise.toml`. Since mise always passes the flag, its default is the only one that ever takes effect and the script's is dead in the normal path — two places to keep in sync for one value, which is the drift shape this whole commit is about. Dropping the flag's `default=` and letting `${HW_PKGS:-…}` be the single source would collapse it (at the cost of `usage_hw` being empty, so you'd pass `HW_PKGS` only when set).
  
  **B4 — nit. `install-base.sh:105`: `$HW_PKGS` unquoted enables globbing as well as splitting.** The `shellcheck disable=SC2086` comment accounts for the intended word-split but not for pathname expansion: a `*` or `?` in the value globs against the ISO's cwd (`/root`). `read -ra hw <<<"$HW_PKGS"` then `"${hw[@]}"` splits without globbing, and pairs with the `--` from A1-new.
  
  **B5 — nit. Two comments now overstate deploy's reach after A3's allow-list.** `system/packages:2` — "system/deploy converges pacman onto this file on each run" — and `install-base.sh:20` — "system/deploy enforces that file on every box" — are both true only of the four allow-listed hosts. Small, but the allow-list is a deliberate safety property and these two sentences read as though it isn't there.
  
  **B6 — nit (pre-existing, now compounded). `system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1:2-3` is wrong in mechanism.** It says *"Arch has no /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 by default, so polkit falls back to the built-in 'other' stack (password only)."* Arch does ship `/usr/lib/pam.d/polkit-1` — verified, it is four `include system-auth` lines — so polkit uses that vendor stack, not the built-in `other`. The *effect* the sentence describes (password only, no fingerprint offered) is correct, so nothing behaves differently. Flagging it because the amendment added ten lines directly beneath it without correcting it, and because B1's false claim grows from the same misconception about where Arch keeps packaged PAM stacks. Fixing both together is one edit.
  
  **B7 — no finding. Split faithfulness confirmed** (see table). Also confirmed the two format claims the new comments make: `pacman -Qq` does resolve virtual provides (`pacman -Qq sh` → `bash`) and does **not** resolve groups (`pacman -Qq vulkan-devel` → "package … was not found"), so `system/packages:25-27` is accurate, including the warning that a group line would read as missing every run.
  
  **B8 — no finding on the amended commit message, with one inherited caveat.** It is materially more precise than round 1's: "unchanged as text, but not in effect" is exactly right; the harmful/inert framing matches the code; the `--` / no-`--noconfirm` / no-`-y` / warn-not-abort paragraph each match what `deploy` actually does; the kernel rationale is sound; "utsuho and fujiwara are AMD" matches `flake.nix:62,84`. It does **not** repeat B1's false ordering claim, so that falsehood is confined to deploy's comment. The single caveat is the zsh omission noted in B2.
  
  **B9 — nit. Discoverability.** `mise.toml`'s `system:deploy` description still reads "Install missing host packages and system-level files…" with no hint that the package half is allow-listed and skippable. Adding "(allow-listed hosts; `SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES=1` to skip)" would put the two new behaviours where a reader of `mise tasks` will find them.

  ## Bottom line
  
  Nine of the twelve fixes hold cleanly, and A4 and A5 in particular are now better-documented than I asked for. Three things to act on before this lands:
  
  1. **B1** — the ordering comment documents a mechanism that does not exist, and contradicts `system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1:2`. Highest-value fix; it's a comment-only edit, and B6 rides along with it.
  2. **A2-new / A1-new** — `HW_PKGS` is the one new untrusted-shaped input in the change, and it passes through both an unquoted remote shell string and a `pacstrap` argv with no `--`. Both are small, local fixes.
  3. **A3-new** — `${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}` falls back to a binary absent from these hosts and absent from both package lists; `uname -n` is the repo's own convention three other places.
  
  **B2** (zsh) is latent and a judgement call, but it is the only entry the new split's rule misfiles, so it's worth a decision rather than a silent pass. Everything else is nit-level.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Base Arch install for a new host, run as root on the archiso live system:
#   HOST=<name> DISK=/dev/nvme0n1 bash install-base.sh
# Normally invoked via `mise run host:install <ip> <host>`.
# Full-disk LUKS2 -> btrfs, systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user sauyon.
# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
# unattended.
set -euo pipefail

DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
ESP=$(part 1)
CRYPT=$(part 2)
HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}
TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}

# wrong rather than merely unused on the other architecture, which is why they
# are NOT in system/packages -- system/deploy enforces that file on every box and
# must not push Intel drivers at the AMD ones. Two of our hosts are AMD
# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.

# before anything touches the disk, so a missing or unparseable list fails while
# the target is still intact.
#   system/packages            what every host must have; system/deploy enforces
#                              the same file on every run afterwards.
#   install/packages-install-only  fresh-install scaffolding, never re-enforced.
# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done
  echo "install-base.sh: no readable package list at any of: $*" >&2
  return 1

mapfile -t boot_pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages-install-only")

[ ${#boot_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: packages-install-only parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

for sv in @ @home @nix @log @cache; do btrfs subvolume create "/mnt/$sv"; done

mount -o "$opts,subvol=@" /dev/mapper/root /mnt

mount -o "$opts,subvol=@home" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/home
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@nix" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/nix
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@log" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/log
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@cache" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/cache
mount -o umask=0077 "$ESP" /mnt/boot

id=${ssid}
type=wifi
autoconnect=true

mode=infrastructure
ssid=${ssid}

[wifi-security]
key-mgmt=wpa-psk

[ipv4]
method=auto

[ipv6]
method=auto

hwclock --systohc

printf 'LANG=en_US.UTF-8\nLC_TIME=en_DK.UTF-8\n' > /etc/locale.conf

printf '127.0.0.1\tlocalhost\n::1\t\tlocalhost\n127.0.1.1\t${HOST}.localdomain\t${HOST}\n' >> /etc/hosts

echo 'KEYMAP=us' > /etc/vconsole.conf
sed -i 's/^HOOKS=.*/HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)/' /etc/mkinitcpio.conf
mkinitcpio -P

bootctl install
cat > /boot/loader/loader.conf <<EOF
default arch.conf
timeout 3
editor no
EOF

title   Arch Linux
linux   /vmlinuz-linux
initrd  /initramfs-linux.img
options rd.luks.name=${luks_uuid}=root rd.luks.options=discard root=/dev/mapper/root rootflags=subvol=@ rw
EOF

echo '%wheel ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel

install -m755 /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/devel/dotfiles/install/bootstrap /mnt/usr/local/bin/bootstrap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Base Arch install for a new host, run as root on the archiso live system:
#   HOST=<name> DISK=/dev/nvme0n1 bash install-base.sh
# Normally invoked via `mise run host:install <ip> <host>`.
# Full-disk LUKS2 -> btrfs, systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user sauyon.
# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
# unattended.
set -euo pipefail

DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
ESP=$(part 1)
CRYPT=$(part 2)
HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}
TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}

# Hardware packages, overridable per host. These are the ones that would be
# wrong rather than merely unused on the other architecture, which is why they
# are NOT in system/packages -- system/deploy enforces that file on every box and
# must not push Intel drivers at the AMD ones. Two of our hosts are AMD
# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.
#   HW_PKGS='amd-ucode vulkan-radeon libva-mesa-driver' mise run host:install ...
HW_PKGS=${HW_PKGS:-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}

# Two package lists, both resolved HERE -- before the passphrase prompts and
# before anything touches the disk, so a missing or unparseable list fails while
# the target is still intact.
#   system/packages            what every host must have; system/deploy enforces
#                              the same file on every run afterwards.
#   install/packages-install-only  fresh-install scaffolding, never re-enforced.
# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done
  echo "install-base.sh: no readable package list at any of: $*" >&2
  return 1
}

mapfile -t pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages" "$here/../system/packages")
mapfile -t boot_pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages-install-only")
# mapfile reports success whatever the process substitution did -- `set -e` does
# not see inside one -- so the counts are checked by hand. Without this an empty
# list pacstraps almost nothing, and the first sign of trouble is arch-chroot
# failing for want of a shell, long after the disk has been wiped.
[ ${#pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: system/packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ${#boot_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: packages-install-only parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

# Refuse to touch a disk that already has partitions; wipe it by hand first
# (sgdisk -Z) if you really mean it.
[[ -b $DISK ]] || { echo "$DISK is not a block device" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $(lsblk -no NAME "$DISK" | wc -l) -eq 1 ]] || { echo "$DISK already has partitions" >&2; exit 1; }
lsblk -dno NAME,SIZE,MODEL "$DISK"

ask() {
  local a b
  while :; do
    read -rsp "$1: " a; echo >&2
    read -rsp "$1 (again): " b; echo >&2
    [[ -n $a && $a == "$b" ]] && break
    echo "empty or didn't match, try again" >&2
  done
  printf '%s' "$a"
}
luks_pass=$(ask "Disk passphrase")
user_pass=$(ask "Password for $USERNAME")

timedatectl set-ntp true

sgdisk -Z "$DISK"
sgdisk -n1:0:+1G -t1:EF00 -c1:EFI -n2:0:0 -t2:8309 -c2:cryptroot "$DISK"
partprobe "$DISK"; udevadm settle

printf '%s' "$luks_pass" | cryptsetup open --key-file - --allow-discards \
  --perf-no_read_workqueue --perf-no_write_workqueue --persistent "$CRYPT" root

mkfs.fat -F32 -n EFI "$ESP"
mkfs.btrfs -f -L "$HOST" /dev/mapper/root

mount /dev/mapper/root /mnt
for sv in @ @home @nix @log @cache; do btrfs subvolume create "/mnt/$sv"; done
umount /mnt
opts=noatime,compress=zstd:1,space_cache=v2
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@" /dev/mapper/root /mnt
mkdir -p /mnt/{boot,home,nix,var/log,var/cache}
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@home" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/home
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@nix" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/nix
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@log" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/log
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@cache" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/cache
mount -o umask=0077 "$ESP" /mnt/boot

pacstrap -K /mnt "${pkgs[@]}" "${boot_pkgs[@]}" "${hw_pkgs[@]}"

genfstab -U /mnt >> /mnt/etc/fstab

# Carry the live system's Wi-Fi over as a NetworkManager connection.
psk_file=$(ls /var/lib/iwd/*.psk | head -1)
ssid=$(basename "$psk_file" .psk)
pass=$(sed -n 's/^Passphrase=//p' "$psk_file")
install -m600 /dev/stdin "/mnt/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/${ssid}.nmconnection" <<EOF
[connection]
id=${ssid}
type=wifi
autoconnect=true

[wifi]
mode=infrastructure
ssid=${ssid}

[wifi-security]
key-mgmt=wpa-psk
psk=${pass}

[ipv4]
method=auto

[ipv6]
method=auto
EOF

arch-chroot /mnt /bin/bash -euo pipefail <<CHROOT

sed -i 's/^#en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/; s/^#en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/' /etc/locale.gen

printf 'LANG=en_US.UTF-8\nLC_TIME=en_DK.UTF-8\n' > /etc/locale.conf
echo ${HOST} > /etc/hostname
printf '127.0.0.1\tlocalhost\n::1\t\tlocalhost\n127.0.1.1\t${HOST}.localdomain\t${HOST}\n' >> /etc/hosts

echo 'KEYMAP=us' > /etc/vconsole.conf
sed -i 's/^HOOKS=.*/HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)/' /etc/mkinitcpio.conf
mkinitcpio -P

bootctl install
cat > /boot/loader/loader.conf <<EOF
default arch.conf
timeout 3
editor no
EOF
cat > /boot/loader/entries/arch.conf <<EOF
title   Arch Linux

initrd  /initramfs-linux.img
options rd.luks.name=${luks_uuid}=root rd.luks.options=discard root=/dev/mapper/root rootflags=subvol=@ rw

chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
# Passwordless sudo only until "mise run bootstrap" finishes; it deletes this.

# Key-only SSH for sauyon, for running bootstrap from another machine.

systemctl enable NetworkManager sshd systemd-timesyncd fstrim.timer bluetooth power-profiles-daemon systemd-oomd
CHROOT

# authorized_keys lives on the live system, not inside the chroot.
install -m600 -o 1000 -g 1000 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/.ssh/authorized_keys

# Clone the dotfiles and add a `bootstrap` command, so after reboot the whole
# second stage is: log in, type bootstrap.

[tasks.bootstrap]
description = "Set up this host: Determinate Nix, sops key via Keycloak sign-in (URL + QR), system:deploy, home-manager switch, tailscale. Fresh box: bootstrap or curl -fsSL ko.ag/bootstrap | bash"
tools = { sops = "latest" }
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
host="$(uname -n)"; host="${host%%.*}"
repo="{{config_root}}"
# install-base.sh leaves passwordless sudo for this; drop it however we exit.
trap 'sudo -n rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

if [ ! -d /nix/var/nix/profiles/default ]; then
  curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
    | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh

# sops key. sops-nix, system/deploy and `mise run sops` read
# ~/.config/sops/gcp-key.json. A new host fetches it from the cluster: a
# Keycloak device-code sign-in (URL + QR, approve on your phone, nothing to
# type), then the resulting token reads Secret bootstrap/sops-gcp-key from the
# apiserver. The Secret is put there once, from a host that has the key:
#   kubectl create namespace bootstrap
#   kubectl -n bootstrap create secret generic sops-gcp-key --from-file=gcp-key.json=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json
key="$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json"
if [ ! -s "$key" ]; then
  nixbin() { echo "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$repo" "nixpkgs#$1^bin")/bin/$1"; }
  jq="$(nixbin jq)"; qrencode="$(nixbin qrencode)"
  issuer="https://keycloak.ko.ag/realms/ko"
  dev="$(curl -fsS -d client_id=kubectl -d 'scope=openid email profile' "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/auth/device")"
  url="$("$jq" -r .verification_uri_complete <<<"$dev")"
  device_code="$("$jq" -r .device_code <<<"$dev")"
  interval="$("$jq" -r '.interval // 5' <<<"$dev")"
  echo
  echo "Sign in to fetch the sops key: $url"
  "$qrencode" -t ansiutf8 "$url"
  echo "Waiting for approval..."
  while :; do
    sleep "$interval"
    tok="$(curl -sS -d client_id=kubectl -d "device_code=$device_code" \
      -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code \
      "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/token")"
    case "$("$jq" -r '.error // empty' <<<"$tok")" in
      "") break ;;
      authorization_pending) ;;
      slow_down) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
      *) echo "bootstrap: sign-in failed: $("$jq" -r '.error_description // .error' <<<"$tok")" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  id_token="$("$jq" -r .id_token <<<"$tok")"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$key")"
  (
    umask 077
    curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $id_token" \
      https://k8s.ko.ag/api/v1/namespaces/bootstrap/secrets/sops-gcp-key \
      | "$jq" -er '.data["gcp-key.json"]' | base64 -d > "$key.tmp"
  )
  mv "$key.tmp" "$key"
  echo "bootstrap: sops key fetched."
fi

# system/deploy first: it installs the attic netrc, so the switch below pulls
# CI's build of this host instead of compiling it.
"$repo/system/deploy"

if command -v home-manager >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  home-manager switch --flake "$repo#$host"
else
  nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch -b pre-hm --flake "$repo#$host"
fi

sudo tailscale status >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo tailscale up

echo "bootstrap: done. Log in again (or exec zsh -l) to pick up the new profile."
'''

description = "Apply home-manager configuration from this flake"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# home-manager configs are keyed by hostname (see flake.nix homeConfigurations.*:

exec home-manager switch --flake "$HOME/devel/dotfiles#$config" "$@"
'''

# ── New host bootstrap (docs/new-host.md) ─────────────────────────────────────
# host:* run on the machine you're driving the install from and ship scripts
# from install/ to the live ISO, which has no mise. bootstrap runs on the new
# host itself, via the committed bin/mise (`mise generate bootstrap`) until
# home-manager provides mise.

[tasks."host:iso"]
description = "Build the Arch install ISO (auto Wi-Fi, key-only root SSH) into ~/Downloads"
dir = "{{config_root}}/install"
usage = 'flag "--out <dir>" help="Where to put the ISO" default="~/Downloads"'
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
[ -f wifi.env ] || { echo "host:iso: copy install/wifi.env.example to install/wifi.env and fill it in" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f authorized_keys ] || cp ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub authorized_keys
out="${usage_out/#\~/$HOME}"
mkdir -p "$out"
docker run --rm --privileged -v "$PWD:/src:ro" -v "$out:/out" archlinux:latest bash /src/build-iso.sh
'''

[tasks."host:install"]
description = "Install base Arch on a host booted from the ISO (prompts for disk passphrase and password)"
dir = "{{config_root}}/install"
usage = '''
arg "<ip>" help="Address of the host running the live ISO"
arg "<host>" help="Hostname; must match a homeConfigurations entry in flake.nix"
flag "--disk <disk>" help="Target disk; must have no partitions" default="/dev/nvme0n1"
flag "--hw <pkgs>" help="Hardware packages (ucode + video); install-base.sh defaults to Intel"
'''
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ssh_opts=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR)
# Both package lists ride along: install-base.sh reads them from beside itself.
# system/packages is the same file system/deploy converges allow-listed hosts
# onto; packages-install-only is fresh-install scaffolding it never re-enforces.
scp "${ssh_opts[@]}" install-base.sh packages-install-only ../system/packages \
  "root@${usage_ip}:/root/"
# printf %q on every value: this string is evaluated by a root shell on the
# target, and --hw is free text that gets pasted rather than typed. A stray
# quote in it would otherwise close the quoting and make the remainder remote
# root commands. HW_PKGS is forwarded only when --hw was given, so
# install-base.sh's own default stays the single source of truth for it.
cmd=$(printf 'HOST=%q DISK=%q' "${usage_host}" "${usage_disk}")
if [ -n "${usage_hw:-}" ]; then
  cmd+=$(printf ' HW_PKGS=%q' "${usage_hw}")
fi
ssh -t "${ssh_opts[@]}" "root@${usage_ip}" "${cmd} bash /root/install-base.sh"
'''

[tasks.bootstrap]
description = "Set up this host: Determinate Nix, sops key via Keycloak sign-in (URL + QR), system:deploy, home-manager switch, tailscale. Fresh box: bootstrap or curl -fsSL ko.ag/bootstrap | bash"
tools = { sops = "latest" }
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
host="$(uname -n)"; host="${host%%.*}"
repo="{{config_root}}"
# install-base.sh leaves passwordless sudo for this; drop it however we exit.
trap 'sudo -n rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

if [ ! -d /nix/var/nix/profiles/default ]; then
  curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
    | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh

# sops key. sops-nix, system/deploy and `mise run sops` read
# ~/.config/sops/gcp-key.json. A new host fetches it from the cluster: a
# Keycloak device-code sign-in (URL + QR, approve on your phone, nothing to
# type), then the resulting token reads Secret bootstrap/sops-gcp-key from the
# apiserver. The Secret is put there once, from a host that has the key:
#   kubectl create namespace bootstrap
#   kubectl -n bootstrap create secret generic sops-gcp-key --from-file=gcp-key.json=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json
key="$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json"
if [ ! -s "$key" ]; then
  nixbin() { echo "$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$repo" "nixpkgs#$1^bin")/bin/$1"; }
  jq="$(nixbin jq)"; qrencode="$(nixbin qrencode)"
  issuer="https://keycloak.ko.ag/realms/ko"
  dev="$(curl -fsS -d client_id=kubectl -d 'scope=openid email profile' "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/auth/device")"
  url="$("$jq" -r .verification_uri_complete <<<"$dev")"
  device_code="$("$jq" -r .device_code <<<"$dev")"
  interval="$("$jq" -r '.interval // 5' <<<"$dev")"
  echo
  echo "Sign in to fetch the sops key: $url"
  "$qrencode" -t ansiutf8 "$url"
  echo "Waiting for approval..."
  while :; do
    sleep "$interval"
    tok="$(curl -sS -d client_id=kubectl -d "device_code=$device_code" \
      -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code \
      "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/token")"
    case "$("$jq" -r '.error // empty' <<<"$tok")" in
      "") break ;;
      authorization_pending) ;;
      slow_down) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
      *) echo "bootstrap: sign-in failed: $("$jq" -r '.error_description // .error' <<<"$tok")" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  id_token="$("$jq" -r .id_token <<<"$tok")"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$key")"
  (
    umask 077
    curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $id_token" \
      https://k8s.ko.ag/api/v1/namespaces/bootstrap/secrets/sops-gcp-key \
      | "$jq" -er '.data["gcp-key.json"]' | base64 -d > "$key.tmp"
  )
  mv "$key.tmp" "$key"
  echo "bootstrap: sops key fetched."
fi

# system/deploy first: it installs the attic netrc, so the switch below pulls
# CI's build of this host instead of compiling it.
"$repo/system/deploy"

if command -v home-manager >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  home-manager switch --flake "$repo#$host"
else
  nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch -b pre-hm --flake "$repo#$host"
fi

sudo tailscale status >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo tailscale up

echo "bootstrap: done. Log in again (or exec zsh -l) to pick up the new profile."
'''

[tasks.hms]
description = "Apply home-manager configuration from this flake"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# home-manager configs are keyed by hostname (see flake.nix homeConfigurations.*:
# utsuho / setsuna / fujiwara / shiori / mari), not a fixed user name.
config="$(uname -n)"; config="${config%%.*}"
exec home-manager switch --flake "$HOME/devel/dotfiles#$config" "$@"
'''

# Host (pacman) packages that must be PRESENT for this config to work, on every
# Arch box we own. system/deploy converges pacman onto this file on each run, so
# a line added here reaches setsuna/utsuho/shiori on their next
# `mise run system:deploy` -- which is the point. pacstrap's list only ever
# reached the *next* new box, which is how fprintd stayed uninstalled for months
# after being wired up in hyprlock and pam.d.
#
# What belongs here: things that must be root-side, because a user profile
# cannot provide them -- a system systemd unit, a system D-Bus service, a module
# the host's own libraries dlopen by name, firmware, state under /var. Anything
# a user can own belongs in home.nix.
#
# What does NOT belong here, and lives in install/packages-install-only instead:
# anything only a *fresh install* needs. The kernel especially -- enforcing
# `linux` would install a second, stock kernel on a host running linux-lts or
# -zen -- and the shell tools install-base.sh needs before home-manager exists.
# That file is pacstrapped once and never enforced again.
#
# Hardware packages sort by whether being wrong is harmful or merely inert:
# intel-ucode and the Intel video drivers are picked per host and stay inline in
# install-base.sh, because pushing them at the AMD boxes would be wrong; fprintd
# and sof-firmware sit here, because a box without the hardware just never
# exercises them.
#
# Format: one package per line, # comments, blank lines ignored. Package names
# only -- `pacman -Qq` resolves virtual provides (`sh` answers bash) but NOT
# groups, so a group line would read as missing on every single deploy.

# disks: the encrypted btrfs root and the ESP
btrfs-progs
cryptsetup
dosfstools

networkmanager
openssh
sudo

# graphics
mesa

sof-firmware
pipewire
pipewire-pulse
pipewire-alsa
wireplumber

# firmware blobs for the kernel, whichever kernel that is
linux-firmware

# system services
polkit
tpm2-tss
tpm2-tools
bluez
bluez-utils
fwupd
power-profiles-daemon

# host's PAM dlopens pam_fprintd.so by bare name out of /usr/lib/security (see
# etc/pam.d/polkit-1), fprintd itself is a root-run system D-Bus service, and
# its enrollments are root state in /var/lib/fprint. hyprlock's
# fingerprint.enabled (home.nix) reaches the daemon over D-Bus rather than PAM,
# so it silently no-ops when the package is absent.
# Enrolling stays manual and per-host: `fprintd-enroll`, then `fprintd-list`.
fprintd

TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}

# Hardware packages, overridable per host. These are the ones that would be
# wrong rather than merely unused on the other architecture, which is why they
# are NOT in system/packages -- system/deploy enforces that file on every box and
# must not push Intel drivers at the AMD ones. Two of our hosts are AMD
# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.
#   HW_PKGS='amd-ucode vulkan-radeon libva-mesa-driver' mise run host:install ...
HW_PKGS=${HW_PKGS:-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}

# Two package lists, both resolved HERE -- before the passphrase prompts and
# before anything touches the disk, so a missing or unparseable list fails while
# the target is still intact.
#   system/packages            what every host must have; system/deploy enforces
#                              the same file on every run afterwards.
#   install/packages-install-only  fresh-install scaffolding, never re-enforced.
# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done
  echo "install-base.sh: no readable package list at any of: $*" >&2
  return 1
}

# Every name that reaches pacstrap gets checked for a leading dash first.
# pacstrap's own option parsing stops at /mnt and it hands the rest to pacman
# inside the chroot, so a `-`-prefixed entry -- from a mangled list or from a
# pasted --hw -- would be read there as an option (--hookdir= runs arbitrary
# code as root via an alpm hook, --root= and --overwrite= are no better). A `--`
# after /mnt would be the usual answer, but whether pacstrap forwards it to
# pacman rather than choking on it is version-dependent, and this script gets
# exactly one run per machine. Rejecting the input needs no such assumption, and
# happens up here where nothing has touched the disk yet.
check_pkgnames() {
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    case $p in
    -*) echo "install-base.sh: refusing package name starting with '-': $p" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
  done
}

# Word-split HW_PKGS with `read -ra` rather than leaving it unquoted: splitting
# is wanted, globbing against the ISO's cwd is not.
read -ra hw_pkgs <<<"$HW_PKGS"

mapfile -t pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages" "$here/../system/packages")
mapfile -t boot_pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages-install-only")
# mapfile reports success whatever the process substitution did -- `set -e` does
