#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Base Arch install for a new host, run as root on the archiso live system:
#   HOST=<name> DISK=/dev/nvme0n1 bash install-base.sh
# Normally invoked via `mise run host:install <ip> <host>`.
# Full-disk LUKS2 -> btrfs, systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user sauyon.
# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
# unattended.
set -euo pipefail

DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
ESP=$(part 1)
CRYPT=$(part 2)
HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}
TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}

# Hardware packages, overridable per host. These are the ones that would be
# wrong rather than merely unused on the other architecture, which is why they
# are NOT in system/packages -- system/deploy enforces that file on every box and
# must not push Intel drivers at the AMD ones. Two of our hosts are AMD
# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.
#   HW_PKGS='amd-ucode vulkan-radeon libva-mesa-driver' mise run host:install ...
HW_PKGS=${HW_PKGS:-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}

# Two package lists, both resolved HERE -- before the passphrase prompts and
# before anything touches the disk, so a missing or unparseable list fails while
# the target is still intact.
#   system/packages            what every host must have; system/deploy enforces
#                              the same file on every run afterwards.
#   install/packages-install-only  fresh-install scaffolding, never re-enforced.
# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done
  echo "install-base.sh: no readable package list at any of: $*" >&2
  return 1
}

# Every name that reaches pacstrap gets checked for a leading dash first.
# pacstrap's own option parsing stops at /mnt and it hands the rest to pacman
# inside the chroot, so a `-`-prefixed entry -- from a mangled list or from a
# pasted --hw -- would be read there as an option (--hookdir= runs arbitrary
# code as root via an alpm hook, --root= and --overwrite= are no better). A `--`
# after /mnt would be the usual answer, but whether pacstrap forwards it to
# pacman rather than choking on it is version-dependent, and this script gets
# exactly one run per machine. Rejecting the input needs no such assumption, and
# happens up here where nothing has touched the disk yet.
check_pkgnames() {
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    case $p in
    -*) echo "install-base.sh: refusing package name starting with '-': $p" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
  done
}

# Word-split HW_PKGS with `read -ra` rather than leaving it unquoted: splitting
# is wanted, globbing against the ISO's cwd is not.
read -ra hw_pkgs <<<"$HW_PKGS"

mapfile -t pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages" "$here/../system/packages")
mapfile -t boot_pkgs < <(read_pkglist "$here/packages-install-only")
# mapfile reports success whatever the process substitution did -- `set -e` does
# not see inside one -- so the counts are checked by hand. Without this an empty
# list pacstraps almost nothing, and the first sign of trouble is arch-chroot
# failing for want of a shell, long after the disk has been wiped.
[ ${#pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: system/packages parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ${#boot_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: packages-install-only parsed to nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ${#hw_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "install-base.sh: HW_PKGS is empty" >&2; exit 1; }
check_pkgnames "${pkgs[@]}" "${boot_pkgs[@]}" "${hw_pkgs[@]}"

# Refuse to touch a disk that already has partitions; wipe it by hand first
# (sgdisk -Z) if you really mean it.
[[ -b $DISK ]] || { echo "$DISK is not a block device" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $(lsblk -no NAME "$DISK" | wc -l) -eq 1 ]] || { echo "$DISK already has partitions" >&2; exit 1; }
lsblk -dno NAME,SIZE,MODEL "$DISK"

ask() {
  local a b
  while :; do
    read -rsp "$1: " a; echo >&2
    read -rsp "$1 (again): " b; echo >&2
    [[ -n $a && $a == "$b" ]] && break
    echo "empty or didn't match, try again" >&2
  done
  printf '%s' "$a"
}
luks_pass=$(ask "Disk passphrase")
user_pass=$(ask "Password for $USERNAME")

timedatectl set-ntp true

sgdisk -Z "$DISK"
sgdisk -n1:0:+1G -t1:EF00 -c1:EFI -n2:0:0 -t2:8309 -c2:cryptroot "$DISK"
partprobe "$DISK"; udevadm settle

printf '%s' "$luks_pass" | cryptsetup luksFormat --batch-mode --type luks2 --key-file - "$CRYPT"
printf '%s' "$luks_pass" | cryptsetup open --key-file - --allow-discards \
  --perf-no_read_workqueue --perf-no_write_workqueue --persistent "$CRYPT" root

mkfs.fat -F32 -n EFI "$ESP"
mkfs.btrfs -f -L "$HOST" /dev/mapper/root

mount /dev/mapper/root /mnt
for sv in @ @home @nix @log @cache; do btrfs subvolume create "/mnt/$sv"; done
umount /mnt
opts=noatime,compress=zstd:1,space_cache=v2
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@" /dev/mapper/root /mnt
mkdir -p /mnt/{boot,home,nix,var/log,var/cache}
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@home" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/home
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@nix" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/nix
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@log" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/log
mount -o "$opts,subvol=@cache" /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/cache
mount -o umask=0077 "$ESP" /mnt/boot

pacstrap -K /mnt "${pkgs[@]}" "${boot_pkgs[@]}" "${hw_pkgs[@]}"

genfstab -U /mnt >> /mnt/etc/fstab

# Carry the live system's Wi-Fi over as a NetworkManager connection.
psk_file=$(ls /var/lib/iwd/*.psk | head -1)
ssid=$(basename "$psk_file" .psk)
pass=$(sed -n 's/^Passphrase=//p' "$psk_file")
install -m600 /dev/stdin "/mnt/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/${ssid}.nmconnection" <<EOF
[connection]
id=${ssid}
type=wifi
autoconnect=true

[wifi]
mode=infrastructure
ssid=${ssid}

[wifi-security]
key-mgmt=wpa-psk
psk=${pass}

[ipv4]
method=auto

[ipv6]
method=auto
EOF

luks_uuid=$(blkid -s UUID -o value "$CRYPT")

arch-chroot /mnt /bin/bash -euo pipefail <<CHROOT
ln -sf /usr/share/zoneinfo/${TZ_NAME} /etc/localtime
hwclock --systohc
sed -i 's/^#en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/; s/^#en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/' /etc/locale.gen
locale-gen
printf 'LANG=en_US.UTF-8\nLC_TIME=en_DK.UTF-8\n' > /etc/locale.conf
echo ${HOST} > /etc/hostname
printf '127.0.0.1\tlocalhost\n::1\t\tlocalhost\n127.0.1.1\t${HOST}.localdomain\t${HOST}\n' >> /etc/hosts

echo 'KEYMAP=us' > /etc/vconsole.conf
sed -i 's/^HOOKS=.*/HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)/' /etc/mkinitcpio.conf
mkinitcpio -P

bootctl install
cat > /boot/loader/loader.conf <<EOF
default arch.conf
timeout 3
editor no
EOF
cat > /boot/loader/entries/arch.conf <<EOF
title   Arch Linux
linux   /vmlinuz-linux
initrd  /initramfs-linux.img
options rd.luks.name=${luks_uuid}=root rd.luks.options=discard root=/dev/mapper/root rootflags=subvol=@ rw
EOF

useradd -m -G wheel,video,input,tss -s /bin/zsh ${USERNAME}
echo '%wheel ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
# Passwordless sudo only until "mise run bootstrap" finishes; it deletes this.
echo '${USERNAME} ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap

# Key-only SSH for sauyon, for running bootstrap from another machine.
install -d -m700 -o ${USERNAME} -g ${USERNAME} /home/${USERNAME}/.ssh
printf 'PermitRootLogin no\nPasswordAuthentication no\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-keys-only.conf

systemctl enable NetworkManager sshd systemd-timesyncd fstrim.timer bluetooth power-profiles-daemon systemd-oomd
CHROOT

printf '%s:%s\n' "$USERNAME" "$user_pass" | arch-chroot /mnt chpasswd

# authorized_keys lives on the live system, not inside the chroot.
install -m600 -o 1000 -g 1000 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/.ssh/authorized_keys

# Clone the dotfiles and add a `bootstrap` command, so after reboot the whole
# second stage is: log in, type bootstrap.
arch-chroot /mnt sudo -u "${USERNAME}" git clone -q https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles.git "/home/${USERNAME}/devel/dotfiles"
install -m755 /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/devel/dotfiles/install/bootstrap /mnt/usr/local/bin/bootstrap

umount -R /mnt
cryptsetup close root
echo "BASE INSTALL DONE - pull the stick and reboot"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
# unattended.
set -euo pipefail

DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
ESP=$(part 1)
CRYPT=$(part 2)
HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}

# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.

# `-` not `:-`, so HW_PKGS='' is honoured as "no hardware packages" (a VM) rather
# than silently meaning Intel. This default is the only one; the --hw flag in
# mise.toml deliberately has none.
HW_PKGS=${HW_PKGS-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}

# the target is still intact.

#                              the same file on every run afterwards.

here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'

    fi

[connection]
id=${ssid}
type=wifi
autoconnect=true

[wifi]
mode=infrastructure
ssid=${ssid}

[wifi-security]
key-mgmt=wpa-psk
psk=${pass}

[ipv4]
method=auto

[ipv6]
method=auto
EOF

luks_uuid=$(blkid -s UUID -o value "$CRYPT")

ln -sf /usr/share/zoneinfo/${TZ_NAME} /etc/localtime
hwclock --systohc
sed -i 's/^#en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8/; s/^#en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/en_DK.UTF-8 UTF-8/' /etc/locale.gen
locale-gen
printf 'LANG=en_US.UTF-8\nLC_TIME=en_DK.UTF-8\n' > /etc/locale.conf
echo ${HOST} > /etc/hostname
printf '127.0.0.1\tlocalhost\n::1\t\tlocalhost\n127.0.1.1\t${HOST}.localdomain\t${HOST}\n' >> /etc/hosts

echo 'KEYMAP=us' > /etc/vconsole.conf
sed -i 's/^HOOKS=.*/HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)/' /etc/mkinitcpio.conf
mkinitcpio -P

bootctl install
cat > /boot/loader/loader.conf <<EOF
default arch.conf
timeout 3
editor no
EOF
cat > /boot/loader/entries/arch.conf <<EOF
title   Arch Linux
linux   /vmlinuz-linux
initrd  /initramfs-linux.img
options rd.luks.name=${luks_uuid}=root rd.luks.options=discard root=/dev/mapper/root rootflags=subvol=@ rw
EOF

useradd -m -G wheel,video,input,tss -s /bin/zsh ${USERNAME}
echo '%wheel ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/10-wheel
# Passwordless sudo only until "mise run bootstrap" finishes; it deletes this.
echo '${USERNAME} ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap

# Key-only SSH for sauyon, for running bootstrap from another machine.
install -d -m700 -o ${USERNAME} -g ${USERNAME} /home/${USERNAME}/.ssh
printf 'PermitRootLogin no\nPasswordAuthentication no\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-keys-only.conf

systemctl enable NetworkManager sshd systemd-timesyncd fstrim.timer bluetooth power-profiles-daemon systemd-oomd
CHROOT

printf '%s:%s\n' "$USERNAME" "$user_pass" | arch-chroot /mnt chpasswd

# authorized_keys lives on the live system, not inside the chroot.
install -m600 -o 1000 -g 1000 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/.ssh/authorized_keys

# Clone the dotfiles and add a `bootstrap` command, so after reboot the whole
# second stage is: log in, type bootstrap.
arch-chroot /mnt sudo -u "${USERNAME}" git clone -q https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles.git "/home/${USERNAME}/devel/dotfiles"
install -m755 /mnt/home/${USERNAME}/devel/dotfiles/install/bootstrap /mnt/usr/local/bin/bootstrap

umount -R /mnt
cryptsetup close root
echo "BASE INSTALL DONE - pull the stick and reboot"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dry-run the host-packages step of system/deploy and the pre-disk half of
# install-base.sh. Nothing here touches a disk, prompts, or runs pacman for real:
# the deploy block is extracted and run with `sudo` stubbed, and install-base.sh
# is pointed at DISK=/dev/null so it aborts at the block-device guard.
set -uo pipefail
WT=/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/fprintd
S=$(dirname "$0")
pass=0 fail=0

ok()   { pass=$((pass+1)); echo "  PASS: $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail+1)); echo "  FAIL: $1"; }
check() { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 (got '$2', want '$3')"; fi; }
grep_ok() { if grep -qF "$2" <<<"$3"; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 (missing '$2')"; fi; }

# ── extract the deploy block ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -n '/^if \[ -n "\${SKIP_HOST_PACKAGES/,/^fi$/p' "$WT/system/deploy" > "$S/block2.sh"
echo "extracted $(wc -l < "$S/block2.sh") lines of the deploy block"
grep -q '^fi$' "$S/block2.sh" || { echo "EXTRACTION BROKEN"; exit 1; }
echo

# Run the block in a subshell with sudo and uname stubbed.
# $1 = fake uname -n output, $2 = sudo exit status, rest = env assignments
run_block() {
  local host=$1 sudo_rc=$2; shift 2

input.content:
system: converge host packages onto a shared list, and install fprintd

pacstrap's list in install-base.sh was the only place host packages were
declared, and it runs on the live ISO -- so a package added after a host was
built never reached it. fprintd is what that cost: hyprlock's
fingerprint.enabled and etc/pam.d/polkit-1's pam_fprintd were wired up months
ago, but nothing ever installed the daemon, so a fresh shiori has the Goodix
reader (27c6:609c) sitting there with no fprintd, no /var/lib/fprint, and a
fingerprint prompt that silently no-ops.

fprintd cannot come from nix: the host's PAM dlopens pam_fprintd.so by bare
name out of /usr/lib/security, fprintd is a root-run system D-Bus service, and
its enrollments are root state under /var.

Split the declaration by lifetime rather than keeping one list:

  system/packages               what must be PRESENT on a host. system/deploy
                                installs whatever is missing on each run, which
                                is the half that reaches setsuna/utsuho/shiori
                                rather than only the next new box. zsh is here,
                                not below: useradd sets the login shell to the
                                absolute path /bin/zsh, which no nix profile can
                                provide.
  install/packages-install-only base, base-devel, the kernel, and the tools
                                needed before home-manager exists. Pacstrapped
                                once, never re-enforced -- converging `linux`
                                would install a second, stock kernel on a host
                                that had moved to -lts or -zen, run the
                                mkinitcpio hook and fill /boot.
  HW_PKGS / --hw                ucode and video drivers, which would be wrong
                                rather than merely unused on the other
                                architecture. Defaults to Intel; utsuho and
                                fujiwara are AMD, so the runbook says to pass
                                it.

The converge step is deliberately conservative. An explicit host allow-list,
not `command -v pacman`: kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an
Arch-based one would sail through a capability check. The host comes from
`uname -n` like the repo's three other host cases, not $HOSTNAME (inheritable)
or hostname(1) (inetutils, installed nowhere here). `--` before the package
arguments, because the list is data and a leading dash would otherwise be read
as a pacman option under sudo; install-base.sh rejects such names outright,
before it touches the disk, since pacstrap forwards them to pacman in the
chroot. No `--noconfirm`, whose default answer to "replace X with Y?" is yes --
a line that reads as purely additive should not be able to remove a package from
a running host. No `-y`, since refreshing the db and installing without
upgrading is the partial-upgrade footgun. And a pacman failure warns rather than
aborts: nothing later in system/deploy is about packages, least of all the attic
netrc that keeps the next home-manager switch from compiling the world.

Both lists are resolved, asserted non-empty and name-checked before the
passphrase prompts, through command substitution rather than `mapfile < <(...)`
so a partial read aborts instead of silently yielding a subset. --hw reaches the
ISO via printf %q rather than interpolation into a remote root shell string.

PAM wiring is unchanged as text, but not in effect, which is worth saying
plainly: polkit-1's `auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so` was inert while the module
could not be dlopen'd, and installing fprintd makes it live. A fingerprint now
short-circuits system-auth, pam_faillock included, for polkit auth_self. sudo
and TTY login stay password-only. Noted in the stack's comment and the runbook,
along with enrollment staying manual per host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5

  HW_PKGS / --hw                ucode and video drivers, which would be wrong
                                rather than merely unused on the other
                                architecture. Defaults to Intel; utsuho and
                                fujiwara are AMD, so the runbook says to pass
                                it.

not `command -v pacman`: kyuusaku is a box whose OS we do not own, and an
Arch-based one would sail through a capability check. The host comes from
`uname -n` like the repo's three other host cases, not $HOSTNAME (inheritable)
or hostname(1) (inetutils, installed nowhere here). `--` before the package
arguments, because the list is data and a leading dash would otherwise be read
as a pacman option under sudo; install-base.sh rejects such names outright,
before it touches the disk, since pacstrap forwards them to pacman in the
chroot. No `--noconfirm`, whose default answer to "replace X with Y?" is yes --
a line that reads as purely additive should not be able to remove a package from
a running host. No `-y`, since refreshing the db and installing without
upgrading is the partial-upgrade footgun. And a pacman failure warns rather than

netrc that keeps the next home-manager switch from compiling the world.

plainly: polkit-1's `auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so` was inert while the module
could not be dlopen'd, and installing fprintd makes it live. A fingerprint now
short-circuits system-auth, pam_faillock included, for polkit auth_self. sudo
and TTY login stay password-only. Noted in the stack's comment and the runbook,
along with enrollment staying manual per host.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Base Arch install for a new host, run as root on the archiso live system:
#   HOST=<name> DISK=/dev/nvme0n1 bash install-base.sh
# Normally invoked via `mise run host:install <ip> <host>`.
# Full-disk LUKS2 -> btrfs, systemd-boot, NetworkManager, user sauyon.
# Prompts for the disk passphrase and the user's password first, then runs
# unattended.
set -euo pipefail

DISK=${DISK:?set DISK, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1}
part() { [[ $DISK == *[0-9] ]] && echo "${DISK}p$1" || echo "${DISK}$1"; }
ESP=$(part 1)
CRYPT=$(part 2)
HOST=${HOST:?set HOST}
USERNAME=${USERNAME:-sauyon}
TZ_NAME=${TZ_NAME:-America/Los_Angeles}

# Hardware packages, overridable per host. These are the ones that would be
# wrong rather than merely unused on the other architecture, which is why they
# are NOT in system/packages -- system/deploy re-enforces that file on every run
# and must not push Intel drivers at the AMD ones. Two of our hosts are AMD
# (utsuho, fujiwara; see flake.nix), so this gets overridden about as often as
# it does not; docs/new-host.md step 0 says so.
#   HW_PKGS='amd-ucode vulkan-radeon libva-mesa-driver' mise run host:install ...
# `-` not `:-`, so HW_PKGS='' is honoured as "no hardware packages" (a VM) rather
# than silently meaning Intel. This default is the only one; the --hw flag in
# mise.toml deliberately has none.
HW_PKGS=${HW_PKGS-intel-ucode vulkan-intel intel-media-driver}

# Two package lists, both resolved HERE -- before the passphrase prompts and
# before anything touches the disk, so a missing or unparseable list fails while
# the target is still intact.
#   system/packages            what every host must have; system/deploy enforces
#                              the same file on every run afterwards.
#   install/packages-install-only  fresh-install scaffolding, never re-enforced.
# `mise run host:install` scp's both next to this script; a plain repo checkout
# finds system/packages one level up.
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# Strip comments, then split on whitespace so a two-names-on-one-line slip
# becomes two packages rather than one fused, nonexistent name.
#
# Read through a command substitution, NOT a process substitution: `$(...)` puts
# the subshell's failure into the assignment's status, where `set -e` sees it, so
# a read that dies partway through aborts the install. `mapfile < <(...)` would
# report success with however many lines it managed -- and a truncated list is
# worse than an absent one, because pacstrap succeeds on the subset and the
# operator gets BASE INSTALL DONE on a host with no cryptsetup.
read_pkglist() {
  local f
  for f in "$@"; do
    if [ -r "$f" ]; then
      sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d'
      return 0
    fi
  done

key="$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json"

  interval="$("$jq" -r '.interval // 5' <<<"$dev")"

    tok="$(curl -sS -d client_id=kubectl -d "device_code=$device_code" \
      -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code \
      "$issuer/protocol/openid-connect/token")"

      https://k8s.ko.ag/api/v1/namespaces/bootstrap/secrets/sops-gcp-key \

  echo "bootstrap: sops key fetched."

else

fi

echo "bootstrap: done. Log in again (or exec zsh -l) to pick up the new profile."

Confirmed at 5c38bba: both residual nits are closed, and I find nothing Critical or Important in either angle — the change is good to go.

Re-ran the install-base.sh smoke tests myself against the committed tree rather than trusting the earlier run: default → `/dev/null is not a block device` (so both lists resolve and both assertions pass before the disk guard and before the passphrase prompts); `HW_PKGS=''` → same, which is the `-` vs `:-` fix working; `HW_PKGS='--hookdir=/tmp/evil'` → `refusing package name starting with '-'` and no disk-guard message, i.e. rejected strictly earlier. The newline flattening I confirmed by reading only — the sandbox refused every attempt to run that expansion in a nested shell — but `${HW_PKGS//$'\n'/ }` followed by a here-string is unambiguous: every newline becomes a space, `read` gets exactly one line, nothing is lost. No risk there.

**One clause in the mise.toml comment to narrow, your call, nit only.** The zsh half I'll back: zsh does read the `$'...'` form, and for package names and device paths `%q` is a no-op, so that reasoning is sound. But "stdin **has to** stay the terminal: the script prompts for the disk passphrase" claims more than is true — `install/bootstrap:8` already solves exactly this with `[ -t 0 ] || exec </dev/tty`, so a `bash -s` variant could reclaim the tty the same way. The honest version is that it *would need* that trick, and it isn't worth it here, rather than that it's impossible. Either drop "has to" or point at the bootstrap precedent.

**Would the harness catch a package silently dropped by a future edit? Partly, and it decays.** The `comm` against dcaecea's pacstrap set catches a drop only while no *intentional* change shares the commit. The first legitimate addition to `system/packages` makes that assertion fail; the natural response is to re-baseline it; and a re-baseline silently absorbs any accidental drop made in the same edit. It also cannot protect anything that was never in dcaecea's list — fprintd is already carried as an exception in the comparison, so fprintd itself is unguarded today. A version that survives editing asserts properties rather than a snapshot: that the two files are disjoint; that nothing in `packages-install-only` also appears in the enforced file; and that every absolute path install-base.sh hardcodes (today just `/bin/zsh`, via `useradd -s`) is provided by a name in one of them. Those three stay true across future edits, and the third is the one that would have caught the zsh mistake before you found it yourself.

**Yes, the `uname` stub makes the arm-selection assertions weaker than they look, in one specific way.** `system/deploy` calls `uname` twice: `uname -n` at :60 for the host arm, and `uname -s` at :210 to gate the Linux-only tailscaled block. A stub that answers with a hostname regardless of its argument makes `uname -s` return that hostname, so the tailscaled block silently no-ops — meaning any assertion that the script "runs to the end" is asserting a shorter script than production runs, and the warn-and-continue test in particular proves less than it appears to. Have the stub dispatch on `$1` and exec `/usr/bin/uname` for anything but `-n`. Separately, and unavoidably: a stub proves the case/pattern logic but not that the four real hosts return those exact strings — that comes from `/etc/hostname`, which install-base.sh writes — so one read-only `uname -n` per box closes it. And as in round 2, the other half of that arm, what the real pacman db on each host answers, is still unexercised; the `pacman -Qq` loop with the install line replaced by `echo` needs no privileges and is the one thing I'd still run on utsuho, setsuna and fujiwara before the first real deploy.

description = "Setup GCP KMS and Service Account for sops-nix"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT="sauyon-dotfiles"
LOCATION="global"
KEYRING="nix-keyring"
KEY="nix-key"
SA_NAME="nix-secret-manager"
SA_EMAIL="${SA_NAME}@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

gcloud iam service-accounts create "$SA_NAME" --display-name="Nix sops-nix Secret Access" --project="$PROJECT" 2>/dev/null || true

    --keyring="$KEYRING" --location="$LOCATION" \
    --member="serviceAccount:$SA_EMAIL" \

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "$PROJECT" \
    --member="serviceAccount:$SA_EMAIL" \

    --iam-account="$SA_EMAIL" --project="$PROJECT"
'''

[tasks.sops]

[tasks.sops-fix]
description = "Fix sops-nix Docker-created root-owned directories and restart"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# sops-nix templates that Docker may have clobbered with root-owned directories
paths=(
  "$HOME/.config/litellm/config.yaml"
)

needs_fix=false
for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
  if [ -d "$p" ]; then
    echo "fixing root-owned directory: $p"
    needs_fix=true
  fi
done

if [ "$needs_fix" = true ]; then
  for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
    if [ -d "$p" ]; then
      sudo rm -rf "$p"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$p")"
    fi
  done
fi

systemctl --user restart sops-nix
systemctl --user status sops-nix --no-pager || true
'''

# ── New host bootstrap (docs/new-host.md) ─────────────────────────────────────

#!/usr/bin/env bash

docker run --rm --privileged -v "$PWD:/src:ro" -v "$out:/out" archlinux:latest bash /src/build-iso.sh
'''

[tasks."host:install"]
description = "Install base Arch on a host booted from the ISO (prompts for disk passphrase and password)"
dir = "{{config_root}}/install"
usage = '''
arg "<ip>" help="Address of the host running the live ISO"
arg "<host>" help="Hostname; must match a homeConfigurations entry in flake.nix"
flag "--disk <disk>" help="Target disk; must have no partitions" default="/dev/nvme0n1"
flag "--hw <pkgs>" help="Hardware packages (ucode + video); install-base.sh defaults to Intel"
'''
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ssh_opts=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR)
# Both package lists ride along: install-base.sh reads them from beside itself.
# system/packages is the same file system/deploy converges allow-listed hosts
# onto; packages-install-only is fresh-install scaffolding it never re-enforces.
scp "${ssh_opts[@]}" install-base.sh packages-install-only ../system/packages \
  "root@${usage_ip}:/root/"
# printf %q on every value: this string is evaluated by a root shell on the
# target, and --hw is free text that gets pasted rather than typed. A stray
# quote in it would otherwise close the quoting and make the remainder remote
# root commands. HW_PKGS is forwarded only when --hw was given, so
# install-base.sh's own default stays the single source of truth for it.
#
# %q emits bash quoting and root's login shell on the ISO is zsh, which is fine
# here -- for package names and device paths the output is byte-identical to the
# input, and zsh reads the $'...' form bash emits for control characters. Feeding
# the script over stdin would avoid depending on the remote shell at all, but
# stdin has to stay the terminal: the script prompts for the disk passphrase.
cmd=$(printf 'HOST=%q DISK=%q' "${usage_host}" "${usage_disk}")
if [ -n "${usage_hw:-}" ]; then
  cmd+=$(printf ' HW_PKGS=%q' "${usage_hw}")
fi
ssh -t "${ssh_opts[@]}" "root@${usage_ip}" "${cmd} bash /root/install-base.sh"
'''

  issuer="https://keycloak.ko.ag/realms/ko"

  while :; do
